title: Topological Superconductors in Doubly-Coupled Nanowires with Altermagnetism
authors: Hongfa Pan, Haoyang Wang, Wenguang Zhu, Zhenhua Qiao
abstract: We theoretically investigate the possibility of engineering topological superconductivity in doubly coupled nanowires integrating proximity-induced superconductivity and altermagnetism. By tuning experimentally accessible parameters, we find four distinct topological superconducting phases: class D, class BDI, and two phases hosting two Majorana zero modes per end, protected respectively by spin-group and magnetic point-group symmetries. Beyond inheriting the advantages of alternating?magnetism induced topological superconductivity, our system provides multiple tuning knobs (e.g., superconducting phase difference and inter-wire coupling) to control topological properties.
summary: This paper theoretically explores engineering topological superconductors in doubly-coupled nanowires that combine proximity superconductivity and altermagnetism. By tuning parameters like the superconducting phase difference ($\varphi$) and magnetic couplings ($J_{1,2}$), the authors demonstrate the realization of multiple robust TSC phases, including those hosting protected Majorana zero modes. This work provides a versatile platform for designing topological quantum materials.
main_problem: The study theoretically investigates how topological superconductivity (TSC) can be engineered in a novel platform: doubly-coupled nanowires that integrate proximity-induced superconductivity and altermagnetism.
main_result: The system was shown to host four distinct TSC phases, including classes D and BDI, with the ability to realize robust Majorana zero modes protected by specific spin-group or magnetic point-group symmetries.
method: The analysis uses a tight-binding model Hamiltonian solved via Bogoliubov–de Gennes formalism in momentum space, characterizing topological states using symmetry classes and winding numbers.
model_or_system: The physical system is a doubly-coupled semiconducting nanowire platform incorporating superconducting (SC) regions and altermagnetic (AM) regions. The model Hamiltonian $H = H_{w1} + H_{w2} + H_{int}$ describes the coupled two-band superconductor.
key_observables: Topological phase transitions marked by bulk gap closing, the presence of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) at boundaries, and the topological invariant Z.
important_parameters: Tunable parameters include the superconducting phase difference ($\varphi$), inter-wire coupling ($t_0$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and altermagnetism strengths ($J_{1,2}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes proximity coupling to superconductors and altermagnets, and relies on controlling multiple symmetry parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the coupled nanowire platform, energy eigenvalues showing zero-energy states (MZMs), and phase diagrams mapping out topological regimes based on $\varphi$ and $J_{1,2}$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the physical challenge to deriving the Hamiltonian, analyzing how symmetry dictates the topological class (D vs BDI), and finally detailing the tunability of these phases using specific parameter controls.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical blueprint for realizing exotic superconducting states by combining magnetic order (altermagnetism) with superconductivity in low-dimensional structures, which is highly relevant to condensed matter theory involving symmetry protection.
